// purpose: @debuggen/instrumentation - the reversible-instrumentation project (AAP 0.7.1 Group 1). This package owns the instrumentation plan schemas (the authoring `InstrumentationPlanInput` and the normalized `InstrumentationPlan`), the `InstrumentationAdapter` contract and its registry, the six built-in adapters, and the ts-morph function-timing patcher with its hash-recorded backups, conflict detection and cleanup - the only code in the product that writes into a developer's working tree (AAP 0.5.1).
// format: Strict JSON, like tsconfig.base.json and every other tsconfig in this repository: both a JSONC-aware reader (`ts.readConfigFile`) and a bare `JSON.parse` can read it, so no consumer has to know which one to reach for. tsc, ESLint, Vitest, tsup and Prettier all accept comments in a tsconfig, but the rationale for each decision is recorded in the `"// …"` string keys of this object instead. TypeScript ignores unknown TOP-LEVEL keys, which is what makes the convention safe; a `"// …"` key inside `compilerOptions` is a hard error instead (TS5023, "Unknown compiler option"), so every note about a single option lives up here under a `"// compilerOptions.<option>"` key and never beside the option itself.
// layering: Position in the acyclic package graph (AAP 0.2.2): shared -> telemetry -> code-analysis -> instrumentation -> ... -> protocol, so `references` below names exactly the three workspaces package.json depends on (@debuggen/shared, @debuggen/telemetry, @debuggen/code-analysis) and nothing else. ../protocol, ../panel-schema, ../panel-renderer and ../model-provider sit ABOVE this package: a reference to any of them is the cycle the layering exists to prevent - rejected by `tsc -b` (TS6202) and independently forbidden by the `no-restricted-imports` layering block of eslint.config.js.
// typecheck-gate: `pnpm typecheck` (= `pnpm demo:generate && tsc -b`) builds the root tsconfig.json solution file, which references every workspace project - this one after packages/shared, packages/telemetry and packages/code-analysis - so the options below are what that blocking gate (AAP 0.8.5) runs on. A misconfiguration here fails the whole monorepo typecheck, not just this package. `pnpm --filter @debuggen/instrumentation typecheck` runs the same `tsc -b` for this project and its three dependencies alone.
// inherited: Everything not stated below is inherited from tsconfig.base.json and must stay that way - in particular `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, the no-unused/no-implicit diagnostics, `target`/`lib` ES2023, `skipLibCheck` (which keeps declaration drift in ts-morph's bundled TypeScript and in the `diff` typings out of this gate) and the declaration-emit settings (`declaration`, `declarationMap`, `sourceMap`, `emitDeclarationOnly`, `incremental`). `noEmit` must never be added: TypeScript 6.0.3 rejects a referenced project that disables emit with TS6310 and the whole gate fails. No strictness flag is relaxed here; `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` in particular is load-bearing for a package whose plan normalisation, adapter results, modification chains and ts-morph node lookups are all indexed accesses that must stay `T | undefined`.
// compilerOptions.composite: Already true in the base; restated because the root solution file references this project and a non-composite reference fails `tsc -b` outright (TS6306). Keeping it local means a future edit to the base cannot silently break the gate at this project. It also stays true while tsup builds dist/: the declaration half of that build turns `composite`/`incremental` off in this package's tsup.config.ts (`dts: { compilerOptions: { composite: false, incremental: false } }`) rather than here, so the bundler's needs never cost the solution build its project reference.
// compilerOptions.module: The base defaults to "ESNext" + "bundler" for the bundled/web workspaces and instructs Node-targeted projects to override with NodeNext. This package is Node-only: ts-morph 28.0.0 loads a target project from a real filesystem, the patcher records backups and performs atomic replacements through `node:fs` and the `./node` entry of @debuggen/shared, and the sole consumer is apps/local-service (also NodeNext). package.json declares `"type": "module"`, so this project is type-checked under real Node ESM resolution rather than a bundler approximation. Consequence for every source file in src/**: relative specifiers must carry an explicit ".js" extension (`import { patchFunctionTiming } from "./patch/function-timing.js"`, `import type { InstrumentationAction } from "./schema/plan.js"`), and directory specifiers must name the file. Extensionless relative imports are a compile error here by design (TS2835/TS2834). tsup/esbuild resolve a "./x.js" specifier from a TypeScript importer back to "./x.ts", so the bundle in dist/ is unaffected.
// compilerOptions.rootDir: Per-workspace (the base deliberately leaves it unset), so the declaration tree under .tsbuild/ mirrors src/ exactly: src/index.ts -> .tsbuild/index.d.ts and src/patch/patcher.ts -> .tsbuild/patch/patcher.d.ts, matching the single "." entry the package.json `exports` map advertises under dist/. It also pins the program's boundary: nothing outside src/ may be an input, which is what keeps the mutated fixture corpus under test/ out (see `"// exclude.fixtures"`).
// compilerOptions.types: The base sets no `types` so that one workspace's ambient globals cannot bleed into another. This package needs exactly one: @types/node 24.13.6 (a root devDependency, resolved through the workspace-root node_modules/@types). It types the `node:fs` / `node:path` / `node:crypto` builtins that src/patch/backup-store.ts, src/patch/patcher.ts and src/cleanup.ts use directly and through `@debuggen/shared/node` - whose `createFileExclusive`, `atomicReplaceFile`, `ensureSecureDir` and `readFileNoFollow` surface `Buffer` and errno-bearing error types - `process.env` for $DEBUGGEN_HOME, and `node:child_process`, which src/patch/patcher.test.ts needs to run each failure-injection scenario in a fresh process (AAP 0.5.1). Deliberately no "lib": ["DOM"] override and no "jsx": nothing here runs in a page and this package emits no React. The browser-side signals its adapters plan for are installed by packages/telemetry's page agent; the adapters only describe them, so admitting `window`/`document` would merely legitimise browser globals in a Node-only patcher.
// compilerOptions.not-overridden: NOT overridden: "outDir" / "declarationDir" / "tsBuildInfoFile". The base already anchors them per project with `${configDir}`, which resolves to the directory of THIS file, so declarations and the incremental stamp land in packages/instrumentation/.tsbuild - ignored by .gitignore, .prettierignore and the ignore list in eslint.config.js. A repository-level path would be an output location outside those ignore lists and would leak build artefacts into `git status`; tsc must likewise never write into packages/instrumentation/dist, which belongs to tsup and holds the artefacts the `exports` map points at. NOT set: "baseUrl" / "paths". `@debuggen/shared`, `@debuggen/telemetry` and `@debuggen/code-analysis` resolve through the pnpm workspace symlink and each package's `exports` map plus the project references below, exactly as the runtime and the bundlers resolve them (AAP 0.2.2).
// include: src/** only, and deliberately including the colocated `*.test.ts` files - schema/*.test.ts, feasibility.test.ts, cleanup.test.ts, patch/function-timing.test.ts, patch/patcher.test.ts, patch/conflict.test.ts and adapters/*.test.ts (AAP 0.8.3) - so the typecheck gate covers the tests too: `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` apply to them exactly as they do to sources. It is also precisely what the `instrumentation` Vitest project collects (`packages/instrumentation/src/**/*.test.ts`). The suites import `{ describe, it, expect }` from "vitest" explicitly rather than relying on globals, and vitest resolves from the workspace-root node_modules, so no "vitest/globals" entry is needed in `types`. No "*.tsx" glob: this package emits no JSX.
// exclude: Replaces the base's inherited list, so it is spelled relative to this directory: packages/instrumentation/dist (tsup output), node_modules, and .tsbuild - the last one repeated from the base because TypeScript excludes `outDir` automatically only when `exclude` is absent, so without it the declarations emitted by `tsc -b` would become inputs of the next run.
// exclude.fixtures: test/fixtures/** is the load-bearing entry. test/fixtures/project-a is a deliberately ordinary, standalone project used as *patching input*: it carries its own package.json and tsconfig.json because the patcher builds a ts-morph `Project` from a target project's tsconfig at runtime and the suites exercise exactly that path, running the real patcher and the real cleanup against it. Its files are therefore MUTATED IN PLACE during a test run - transiently holding `__DEBUGGEN__`, `__orig` and the inserted `type __DebuggenSpanHelper` alias - and it also carries constructs the patcher must *reject* (generator and async-generator functions) plus `.js`/`.jsx` variants this project does not compile (`allowJs` is false in the base). If any of that entered this program, `tsc -b` output would depend on test execution order and `strict`/`noUnusedLocals` would fail on fixture code that is intentionally plain. `include` above already restricts the input set to src/**; this entry states the boundary so that widening `include` cannot silently swallow the corpus, and it is the typecheck half of the same exclusion the root vitest.config.ts (`**/test/fixtures/**`) and the ESLint ignore list apply to test collection and lint. The fixture's own tsconfig.json is correspondingly absent from `references` below, so `tsc -b` never builds it.
// references: Exactly the three `@debuggen/*` dependencies package.json declares, listed bottom-up so the order matches the layering `tsc -b` walks: ../shared for ids, `Result`, POSIX path normalisation and containment, the `SourceLocation` schema recorded on every ModificationRecord, and the `./node` hashing and safe-fs entries the backup store writes through; ../telemetry for the TelemetryEvent kinds and signal vocabulary the adapters map their runtime actions onto; ../code-analysis for the code graph src/feasibility.ts queries to confirm a planned file and symbol exist before anything is patched. `tsc -b` builds those projects (packages/shared first of all, since the other two reference it) before this one, which is what proves each published `exports` map - not a source path alias - resolves. Nothing else belongs here.
